noticias.titulo: En 2021, un almirante lanzó una predicción sobre China que hizo temblar a EEUU. Estamos a punto de averiguar si tenía razón: "espero estar equivocado"
noticias.resumen: En marzo de 2021, mientras buena parte del mundo seguía pendiente de la pandemia, un almirante estadounidense compareció ante el Senado para lanzar una advertencia sobre el futuro del Pacífico . Sus palabras acabarían convirtiéndose en una de las referencias más importantes de la planificación militar del Pentágono. Ahora, a las puertas de 2027, aquel almirante ha vuelto a hablar . La predicción que hizo temblar al Pentágono. El 9 de marzo de 2021, Philip Davidson, entonces comandante del Mando Indo-Pacífico de Estados Unidos, advirtió ante el Comité de Servicios Armados del Senado de que…
noticias.contenido: En marzo de 2021, mientras buena parte del mundo seguía pendiente de la pandemia, un almirante estadounidense compareció ante el Senado para lanzar una advertencia sobre el futuro del Pacífico . Sus palabras acabarían convirtiéndose en una de las referencias más importantes de la planificación militar del Pentágono. Ahora, a las puertas de 2027, aquel almirante ha vuelto a hablar . La predicción que hizo temblar al Pentágono. El 9 de marzo de 2021, Philip Davidson, entonces comandante del Mando Indo-Pacífico de Estados Unidos, advirtió ante el Comité de Servicios Armados del Senado de que China estaba acelerando sus ambiciones de sustituir a Estados Unidos como potencia dominante. Y señaló un objetivo especialmente preocupante: Taiwán. “Creo que la amenaza se manifestará durante esta década, de hecho, en los próximos seis años»” afirmó . Aquella declaración dio origen a la denominada "ventana de Davidson" , un horizonte temporal que situaba en 2027 el momento en que China podría estar preparada para lanzar una invasión creíble de la isla. Dos años después, el entonces director de la CIA, William Burns, reforzó aquella evaluación al asegurar que Xi Jinping había ordenado a sus mandos militares estar preparados para invadir Taiwán en 2027. En Xataka EEUU financió una red de sensores en el Pacífico. China ha utilizado sus datos para descubrir una gigantesca estructura invisible bajo el mar “Espero estar equivocado”. Ahora que aquella fecha está a punto de llegar, Davidson ha explicado en el pódcast Why Should We Care About the Indo-Pacific? cómo ha cambiado su evaluación. El almirante, retirado desde 2021, considera que Estados Unidos y sus aliados han adoptado numerosas medidas que podrían haber alterado los cálculos de Pekín. “En el fondo, espero estar equivocado”, ha afirmado . Si China no invade Taiwán, sostiene , podría significar que las recomendaciones de su antiguo mando y las decisiones adoptadas por Washington y otros gobiernos han funcionado. Conviene recordar que Davidson no predijo necesariamente una guerra en 2027, sino una ventana de creciente vulnerabilidad . Y que disponer de la capacidad para invadir la isla no significa haber decidido hacerlo. Un lanzador de capacidad de alcance medio (MRC) llega al norte de Luzón, Filipinas, el 8 de abril de 2024, como parte del primer despliegue de esta capacidad en el teatro de operaciones Estados Unidos ha movido sus fichas. Una de las principales recomendaciones de Davidson en 2021 era transformar el despliegue militar estadounidense en el Pacífico. Washington necesitaba distribuir mejor sus fuerzas y disponer de una mayor capacidad ofensiva desde tierra, mar y aire, en lugar de depender tanto de sus grandes plataformas navales. Desde entonces, Estados Unidos ha desplegado sistemas de misiles y unidades del Ejército y los Marines en Filipinas y otros puntos de la primera cadena de islas, el arco geográfico que se extiende desde Japón hacia Taiwán y Filipinas. También ha intensificado la cooperación con sus aliados. En las recientes maniobras Keen Sword participaron unos 45.000 militares japoneses, 11.000 estadounidenses y fuerzas de otros siete países. El objetivo es complicar enormemente cualquier intento chino de conquistar Taiwán. Philip Davinson El despertar militar de Japón. Davidson considera que uno de los cambios más importantes de estos años ha sido la transformación de Japón . En diciembre de 2022, Tokio aprobó una nueva estrategia de seguridad nacional y emprendió un programa de rearme destinado a elevar su gasto en defensa del 1% al 2% del PIB . También ha desarrollado capacidades espaciales y cibernéticas y reorganizado sus fuerzas terrestres y aéreas en las islas del suroeste, especialmente en el archipiélago de las Ryukyu , próximo a Taiwán. Pero el cambio más significativo es político: Japón ha identificado a China como su principal desafío estratégico y ha estrechado su alianza militar con Washington. A ello se suma AUKUS , el pacto firmado en septiembre de 2021 por Australia, Reino Unido y Estados Unidos para compartir tecnología de submarinos de propulsión nuclear. Taiwán quiere convertirse en un erizo. La propia isla también ha modificado s u estrategia defensiva . Taiwán ha ampliado el servicio militar obligatorio de unos pocos meses a un año y reforzado sus sistemas de preparación ante emergencias. Davidson destaca especialmente el concepto de defensa desarrollado por el almirante taiwanés Lee Hsi-min, basado en compensar la abrumadora superioridad militar china mediante capacidades asimétricas . La idea consiste en desplegar minas navales, drones aéreos y submarinos, embarcaciones no tripuladas, misiles móviles, sistemas antiaéreos portátiles y armamento anticarro para destruir las fuerzas invasoras antes de que puedan consolidar sus desembarcos. En lugar de intentar igualar a China en número de barcos y aviones, Taiwán pretende convertir sus costas en una pesadilla militar. El problema es que, según The War Zone , la isla todavía está lejos de disponer de todas esas capacidades, especialmente en materia de drones . Un aerodeslizador (LCAC) de la Fuerza Marítima de Autodefensa de Japón, asignado al Primer Escuadrón de Guerra Anfibia, entra navegando en el puerto de la Estación Aeronaval del Cuerpo de Marines de Iwakuni, Japón, el 28 de octubre de 2026, durante el ejercicio Keen Sword Una factura de 14.000 millones que sigue pendiente. Pese a los avances, Davidson está especialmente preocupado por la lentitud con la que Estados Unidos suministra armamento a Taiwán. El almirante reclama que Washington entregue en los próximos meses o, como máximo, en un año, los aproximadamente 14.000 millones de dólares en ventas militares comprometidas. El paquete, compuesto principalmente por misiles antiaéreos Patriot PAC-3 y NASAMS, quedó paralizado tras la reunión de mayo entre Donald Trump y Xi Jinping, según informó AP . A las presiones diplomáticas chinas se añade otro problema: las guerras de Oriente Medio y las entregas a Ucrania han reducido las reservas estadounidenses de interceptores. Actualmente, la producción de misiles PAC-3 MSE ronda las 650 unidades anuales, aproximadamente la mitad destinadas a Estados Unidos y el resto a sus aliados. El Pentágono pretende elevar esa cifra hasta los 2.000 interceptores anuales. La distancia de Taiwán al este de China La guerra que ya se está librando. Davidson identifica otro frente que ha empeorado considerablemente desde 2021: la guerra de la información. El almirante acusa a China de intentar socavar los procesos democráticos de Taiwán y erosionar la confianza de los estadounidenses en sus dirigentes políticos, empresariales y militares. Pekín, sostiene , aprovecha accidentes, crisis y controversias para inundar las redes sociales con propaganda, una práctica en la que también participan Rusia, Irán y otros actores. Plus: el almirante menciona estimaciones según las cuales los bots y operadores propagandísticos podrían representar hasta el 70% de los comentarios en determinados hilos de redes sociales. Su conclusión es que Estados Unidos debería invertir tantos esfuerzos en combatir estas operaciones como está dedicando actualmente a los drones y los sistemas autónomos. En Xataka EEUU ha mirado por satélite una fábrica china y ha encontrado algo que no le gusta: cuatro aviones para cambiar la guerra aérea en el Pacífico La ventana está a punto de abrirse. Pese a todo, siguen existiendo interrogantes que Davidson no ha abordado . Por ejemplo, ¿intervendría realmente Estados Unidos si unas maniobras militares chinas alrededor de Taiwán se transformaran repentinamente en una invasión? ¿Dispondría de tiempo suficiente para reaccionar? ¿Podrían los misiles chinos mantener alejadas a las fuerzas estadounidenses durante las primeras fases del conflicto? Y, sobre todo, ¿estaría dispuesta la sociedad estadounidense a asumir el coste humano de una guerra contra China? Mientras Pekín continúa ampliando sus capacidades militares y aumentando la presión sobre Taiwán, las respuestas siguen sin estar claras. En 2021, Davidson dio al Pentágono seis años para prepararse ante una amenaza que parecía relativamente lejana. Ahora, esos seis años están a punto de cumplirse. Y el hombre que puso fecha al peligro espera que todo el trabajo realizado desde entonces sirva para demostrar que estaba equivocado. China lo acaba de construir y le ha quitado hasta el piloto En Xataka | China ha inventado un Frankenstein para sus cementerios de palas eólicas: una descarga de medio segundo para resucitarlas como grafeno - La noticia En 2021, un almirante lanzó una predicción sobre China que hizo temblar a EEUU. noticias.contenido: With the UK release of You Can See Everything looming, now’s an ideal time to get up to speed on the bizarre, puckish and very meta comedic oeuvre of its star “There are three sides to every story: your side, my side, and the truth. And no one is lying. Memories shared serve each differently.” Those words were spoken by film producer Robert Evans – but nobody has ever interrogated the idea more skilfully than comedian Nathan Fielder. The three-hour documentary You Can See Everything – co-directed by and starring Fielder – opens in the UK on Friday, having already become an unlikely cultural phenomenon and box office sensation in the US. The film follows disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes in the weeks leading up to her beginning a prison sentence for defrauding investors; what emerges is a profound meditation on the nature of truth and the fundamental unknowability of other human beings. To view the film as being simply about the Theranos scandal is akin to considering Casablanca merely a movie about a nightclub. And, as one might expect given Fielder’s background, it’s hilarious. noticias.titulo: Un oso pardo ha encontrado su nuevo hogar en un pueblo asturiano. El problema es que sus vecinos no lo quieren allí
noticias.resumen: En Villatresmil, parroquia del concejo asturiano de Tineo, anochece temprano y en plena oscuridad ronda por la zona un nuevo inquilino de más de cien kilos. Según 20minutos , los vecinos aseguran que un oso pardo se pasea por las noches entre las casas y que se lo encuentran a las puertas. Y quizá el oso Yogui era muy gracioso cuando se embadurnaba en miel robada, o Winnie de Pooh no mataría ni a una mosca, pero este oso que ya se ha colado en varios corrales no está haciendo gracia a nadie. Algunos, cuenta el medio, salen con petardos en el bolso para intentar asustarlo ( no sirve de mucho…
noticias.contenido: En Villatresmil, parroquia del concejo asturiano de Tineo, anochece temprano y en plena oscuridad ronda por la zona un nuevo inquilino de más de cien kilos. Según 20minutos , los vecinos aseguran que un oso pardo se pasea por las noches entre las casas y que se lo encuentran a las puertas. Y quizá el oso Yogui era muy gracioso cuando se embadurnaba en miel robada, o Winnie de Pooh no mataría ni a una mosca, pero este oso que ya se ha colado en varios corrales no está haciendo gracia a nadie. Algunos, cuenta el medio, salen con petardos en el bolso para intentar asustarlo ( no sirve de mucho ). El Ayuntamiento reclama a la Consejería de Medio Rural medidas “urgentes y eficaces”. Qué ha pasado. Según el Ayuntamiento , el animal lleva días en Villatresmil y pueblos cercanos: ha entrado en una panera, ha recorrido calles, ha dañado alguna vivienda y se ha subido a frutales. La alcaldesa, Montse Fernández, dice que la gente tiene miedo de salir, sobre todo al atardecer. Un vecino contó que el primer día el oso entró en su finca hacia las diez y media de la noche y derribó una colmena sobre el hórreo , y al día siguiente tiró el cobertizo de otra casa. Las dos versiones del calendario. Para los vecinos, la situación está durando semanas. Pero el Principado tiene el registro del aviso al 112 del 4 de noviembre , no antes. Ese mismo día los agentes de la Patrulla Oso acudieron al pueblo. Hubo vigilancia activa, métodos disuasorios, cámaras de videovigilancia y, el 6 de noviembre, una trampa tipo culvert para capturarlo . Asegura que desde esa fecha no se ha vuelto a ver al animal en el núcleo rural y que no es un oso problemático ni habituado a las personas. Los vecinos, a día de hoy, siguen hablando de un desasosiego generalizado y abandono institucional. En Xataka Mientras discutimos qué especie introducir, el oso pardo sigue expandiéndose por el noroeste de la península Ibérica Por qué no se puede “echar”. El oso pardo está catalogado en peligro de extinción en España y en Asturias, y su especie figura en los anexos de la Directiva de Hábitats . La ley del Patrimonio Natural prohíbe dar muerte, dañar, molestar o inquietar adrede a los animales silvestres. El Código Penal castiga matarlos, y la Fiscalía ha pedido 2 años de cárcel para un acusado de matar a un oso con un lazo. Es la pena máxima para estos casos. Asturias dispone además de un plan de recuperación que obliga a mantener una patrulla móvil especializada. La especie, eso sí, se está recuperando. La población cantábrica se estimó en 370 ejemplares en 2020-2021 , frente a los 80-100 de los años noventa, y la Fundación Oso de Asturias cree que ya supera los 400 . Y más osos significa más encuentros con pueblos. El protocolo. Lo que sí existe es un Protocolo para la intervención con osos en la cordillera cantábrica , aprobado en 2019 por las cuatro comunidades y el Ministerio. Primero se vigila y se ahuyenta. Si no basta, se captura al oso con trampas, se le toman muestras y se le coloca un crotal y un collar GPS, para recuperarlo en el mismo sitio o lo más cerca posible si escapa. La captura, según el Principado, es en sí una herramienta de disuasión. Ya en 2025 se reubicaron seis osos habituados a pueblos. Qué piden unos y otros. La organización URA, que representa a ganaderos, considera que oso y lobo se han recuperado lo suficiente como para revisar los protocolos y permitir más control de la especie ; su coordinador habla de ocho ataques en un mes a una misma ganadería de Villatresmil. Fapas replica que el oso sigue siendo frágil (más que el lobo, al menos). Su director honorario, Roberto Hartasánchez, ve un problema de gestión administrativa y no de conservación, y cree que podría capturarse al ejemplar sin cambiar los protocolos. En Xataka Hay una batalla sin cuartel entre los ganaderos de España y la industria del turismo por una nueva realidad: los osos Los vecinos. Llamar al 112 Asturias es la primera medida. Revisar contenedores, comederos de ganado y frutales, que son su reclamo, la segunda. El Principado, junto a las fundaciones Oso Pardo y Oso de Asturias, ofrece pastores eléctricos para huertas, colmenas y cuadras. Y si hay encuentro, la Fundación Oso Pardo aconseja que el oso te vea y te oiga, pero sin gritar ni correr, y retirarse despacio. Sin embargo, los vecinos de la región no están dispuestos a asumir que un solo viva a su lado. Cómo lo hacen en otros sitios. En la Columbia Británica canadiense, los osos protagonizan unas 20.000 llamadas al año al Servicio de Agentes de Conservación, y la basura es el principal reclamo. Pero a ver, son animales mucho más grandes en regiones más pobladas. Las autoridades insisten en que reubicar al animal rara vez funciona , porque suele volver o convertirse en problema en otro pueblo. Por eso la apuesta son los programas Bear Smart y las ordenanzas sobre residuos, y los osos ya habituados a la comida humana acaban sacrificados : 2.490 osos negros entre 2015 y 2019. En Colorado rige la política de “dos aviso”: el oso que se mete en una casa o en un contenedor se captura, se marca con una etiqueta en la oreja y se traslada, y si reincide se le sacrifica. En 2025, 52 osos fueron reubicados y 78 sacrificados , y este año, por la sequía, el sacrificio se ha cuadruplicado hasta casi 300 a finales de agosto. A cambio, la ley estatal castiga ahora a quien deje basura accesible sin esperar a que el oso la toque, con multas de hasta 5.000 dólares en la tercera infracción. La diferencia con Asturias es de escala y de estatus. Esos osos son negros y se cuentan por decenas de miles ; el oso cantábrico apenas alcanza los 400 ejemplares y solo se reubica en casos puntuales . En Rumanía, con unos 11.500 osos frente a los 4.000 de 2007 , tienen una ley que prevé abatir 859 al año entre 2026 y 2027 , avalada por su Tribunal Constitucional. Pero claro, cuando Eslovaquia anunció que abatiría 350 osos, un eurodiputado español señaló que esa cifra equivale a toda la población de España . No es comparable. noticias.contenido: El fraude eléctrico ya no es lo que era (es decir, un vecino haciendo un puente a una PIA del cuadro de contadores). Ya contamos cómo Endesa usa la IA contra las plantaciones de marihuana y cómo cazó a 16 restaurantes de Barcelona con los vídeos de unos influencers. Y Málaga es el último retrato de esa profesionalización: en los 10 primeros meses de 2026, e-distribución, la filial de redes de Endesa, ha detectado más de 3.900 fraudes en la provincia. 13 al día. La energía asociada suma 33 millones de kWh, el consumo de más de 9.500 hogares. ¿Y quién lo paga? Una plantación por semana. Entre enero y octubre, e-distribución desmanteló en Málaga, junto a las fuerzas de seguridad, 43 fraudes ligados a plantaciones de marihuana. Suman 4,5 millones de kWh, el 14% de la energía defraudada. Haciendo la cuenta, son el 1% de los casos y cada uno defrauda unos 105.000 kWh, 14 veces más que el resto, que ronda los 7.400. Endesa calcula que una plantación consume como 80 viviendas: es como si un bloque entero se colgara de un solo enganche. Además, según el Informe Europeo sobre Drogas 2026 , España concentró en 2024 el 75% de las plantas de cannabis incautadas en toda la UE. Fusibles y reconexiones. Málaga vive un momento tensionado: a un lado de la ladera, los nómadas digitales desequilibrando la economía local. Abajo, en los barrios periféricos, los cultivos de marihuana suponen el 13% de ese consumo. Pero estos robos generan problemas extra: un enganche sobrecarga la red y saltan las protecciones ante averías (no para consumo diario). En las peores zonas se funden hasta 15 fusibles al día y se corta la luz a todos los clientes del tramo, casi todos con contrato. Subir la potencia no arregla nada: en algunos sitios ya multiplica por 5 la necesaria y el consumo ilegal vuelve a saturarla. A cada desconexión, una reconexión, a menudo de varias horas. Cómo los detectan. Contadores inteligentes y sensores de la red generan datos, y modelos de machine learning y deep learning buscan consumos anómalos. Esa IA encuentra robo en una de cada dos inspecciones, el doble que en 2017. Los avisos ciudadanos completan el cuadro: entre enero y septiembre, e-distribución recibió 51.010 en toda España y de ahí salieron cerca de 29.000 inspecciones. Desde 2025 trabaja además con la Policía Nacional bajo un protocolo de colaboración . La Palma-Palmilla. El caso más visible es este barrio. Endesa intervino allí el 30 de junio y el 7 y el 15 de julio, con la Policía, y el 78% de lo inspeccionado resultó fraude. Después, terceros manipularon la red para reconectar, y una decena de casas de la calle Doctor Gálvez Moll pasó casi 3 días sin luz. Una vecina contó que su abuela, de casi 90 años, depende de una máquina de oxígeno. FACUA y Con Málaga denuncian que las operaciones criminalizan a una barriada entera. Endesa responde que el riesgo de electrocución y de incendio justifica actuar. Qué dice el Código Penal. El artículo 255 castiga con multa de 3 a 12 meses defraudar fluido eléctrico. Si no pasa de 400 euros, la multa baja a entre 1 y 3 meses. La Ley Orgánica 1/2026 cambió el panorama para las plantaciones. Desde el 10 de abril, un nuevo 255.3 impone prisión de 6 a 18 meses o multa de 12 a 24 meses al enganche que abastece instalaciones del artículo 368, sea cual sea la cuantía. En Xataka La Guardia Civil detiene a un hombre que alquiló un chalet en Madrid, pinchó la luz y lo convirtió en un indoor con 391 plantas de marihuana Por cierto, la nueva ley no es retroactiva: los hechos anteriores se juzgan con la ley vieja. El cultivo en sí ya era delito, con 1 a 3 años de cárcel para el cannabis, y más si la cantidad es notoria (no como la del chico vasco que solo tenía para consumo propio). La vía eléctrica. Al margen del juzgado, la distribuidora tiene sus armas. El artículo 52.6 de la Ley 24/2013 del Sector Eléctrico y el artículo 87 del Real Decreto 1955/2000 le permiten suspender el suministro de forma inmediata ante un enganche sin contrato. También facturar: sin criterio objetivo, cobra la potencia por 6 horas diarias durante un año. El artículo 90 resuelve el contrato de forma automática. El Defensor del Pueblo critica que la compañía fije por su cuenta la cantidad y el corte, sin audiencia al interesado. Un vacío, según Endesa. Fuera de las plantaciones, el resto de fraudes solo acarrea multa. En Francia, Portugal, Italia o Alemania, recuerda la compañía, puede conllevar prisión incluso en su modalidad básica. Ya criticaba la Fiscalía General, en su memoria de 2025, que el delito se quede en multa. Aunque las consecuencias operan en todas direcciones: las agresiones a técnicos de e-distribución y de sus contratas se multiplicaron por más de 3 desde 2024. Aunque son meros trabajadores, este año ya superan en cerca de un 20% las de todo 2025. noticias.titulo: Xi Jinping y Vladimir Putin se reúnen en China en la antesala del encuentro trilateral con Donald Trump
noticias.resumen: Los líderes se congregan en el marco de la cumbre del foro de Cooperación Asia-Pacífico (APEC); el presidente de Estados Unidos se encuentra en Filipinas y viajará este miércoles a Shenzhen
noticias.contenido: SHENZHEN.- Los presidentes de China y Rusia, Xi Jinping y Vladimir Putin, iniciaron este miércoles una reunión en Shenzhen , un día antes de la histórica cita tripartita que sostendrán junto con su par de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump . Las conversaciones, que se llevan a cabo al margen de la cumbre del foro de Cooperación Asia-Pacífico (APEC), marcan la quinta vez que ambos líderes se congregan en este año. Antes de tener la reunión, Putin, que aterrizó este martes en China para participar de la cumbre, se refirió al encuentro que tendrán este jueves los tres mandatarios y sostuvo que se tratará de un evento “muy útil ”. “En un mundo contemporáneo lleno de turbulencias, en medio de la fragmentación de la economía global y en un momento en que los riesgos político-militares van en aumento, lo que se necesita desesperadamente es unidad en lugar de división”, añadió ante empresarios en la APEC. Según el mandatario ruso, son además necesarios “igualdad en lugar de hegemonía, colaboración en lugar de aislamiento y diálogo en lugar de ultimátums”. President Donald J. Trump and Philippine President @bongbongmarcos hold a bilateral meeting: "I very much appreciate your welcoming me, and us, back to the Philippines as we reaffirm one of America's oldest and most important alliances in the Pacific." pic.twitter.com/amaTIYZPz4 — The White House (@WhiteHouse) November 18, 2026 Putin también señaló que las sanciones occidentales impuestas a Moscú desde su invasión de Ucrania en 2022 han “fracasado” y que Rusia salió adelante “con dignidad”. Por otro lado, este mismo martes, Trump comenzó su gira por Asia y aterrizó en Manila , Filipinas, donde fue recibido por el presidente local, Ferdinand Marcos Jr. El mandatario republicano mantiene una reunión bilateral con su par, en la que expresó: “Me complace mucho que me hayas dado la bienvenida de regreso a Filipinas mientras reafirmamos una de las alianzas más antiguas e importantes de Estados Unidos en el Pacífico”. El jefe de Estado norteamericano, en tanto, partirá este miércoles a Shenzhen, en donde continuará con su gira por Asia. El jueves participará, en primer lugar, de un encuentro bilateral con Xi Jinping y, luego, tendrá otra reunión en la que se sumará Putin. El viaje de Trump a Asia se da luego de una dura derrota en las elecciones intermedias y en busca de conseguir cambios importantes. En su gira, el mandatario se dispone a mantener una reunión inédita y apuesta a una diplomacia sin guiones. Hace un año, Trump aprovechó un viaje similar a Asia para acordar una tregua comercial con China y asegurar compromisos de inversión de Japón y Corea del Sur. Esta vez, viaja con su partido ya sin el control del Congreso a partir de enero y con la atención empezando a centrarse en un grupo de aspirantes presidenciales que buscan reemplazarlo en 2028. ⚡️ On November 17, President of Russia Vladimir #Putin arrived in China on a working visit to attend the 33rd #APEC Summit. pic.twitter.com/emYn0JLTNy — MFA Russia 🇷🇺 (@mfa_russia) November 17, 2026 La reunión trilateral El Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores anunció este domingo el encuentro de los tres líderes a través de un breve comunicado, en el que detalló que uno de los temas que se tratarán será la “paz mundial” . Según indicaron funcionarios estadounidenses, Trump quiere hablar de la reducción del arsenal nuclear y tiene previsto plantear su guerra en Irán, pero no se espera que aborde la guerra de Rusia en Ucrania. En esta línea, el presidente alemán, Frank-Walter Steinmeier , dijo que, en una reunión reciente, Xi Jinping mostró “irritación” cuando surgió la idea de que las conversaciones trilaterales incluyeran el tema de Ucrania. “Señaló explícitamente que se trata de un conflicto europeo en el que los europeos también deben estar en la mesa”, expresó a la cadena ARD . En cuanto al desarme nuclear, China insiste desde hace tiempo en que Estados Unidos y Rusia reduzcan primero sus propios enormes arsenales nucleares antes de acceder a conversaciones sobre su propio arsenal. Con información de AFP y AP.

noticias.resumen: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 18 – An… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. A Medium-Sized […]
noticias.contenido: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 18 – A… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. A Medium-Sized Solar Flare Explanation: What a flare for the chromatic ! Today’s image combines a series of images taken over ten minutes capturing the Sun ’s chromosphere , the layer of the Sun ’s atmosphere above its surface where the temperature rises . Why would the Sun become hotter farther away from its core ? This is potentially due to energy from the swirling magnetic fields extending up through the Sun’s atmosphere. Those same magnetic fields can twist and snap , releasing light and energetic particles as a solar flare . The H-alpha filter used for today’s image captures light from energized hydrogen atoms as they travel off the Sun’s surface during a flare on May 14, 2025. This flare was classified as an M1 based on GOES observations , meaning it was moderately bright in X-rays . M-class flares can cause radio blackouts at Earth’s poles and minor radiation storms that can harm astronauts. They aren’t even the most powerful flares ! NASA, NOAA , and other agencies monitor the Sun to predict and identify such storms so we can protect humans on Earth and in space. noticias.titulo: Sierra Snow Season Spins Up
noticias.resumen: A widespread, early-season snowstorm blanketed California’s mountains in white in mid-November 2026.
noticias.contenido: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Sierra Snow Season Spins Up Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search November 12 November 14 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison November 12 November 14 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison November 12 November 14 Curtain Toggle 2-Up California’s Sierra Nevada got an early taste of wintry weather when one of the first major snowfalls of the water year arrived on November 13, 2026. A moisture-laden storm delivered heavy rains to lower elevations in the Sacramento area and snow accumulations of around a foot to some mountainous areas. The recent bout of wet weather was the first in a quick succession of Pacific storms bringing rain, snow, and wind to the U.S. West in mid-November. The MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Terra satellite captured this image (right) of fresh snow in the Sierra Nevada on the morning of November 14, during a lull between weather systems. Two days earlier (left), the mountains were mostly bare, with snow appearing only at the highest elevations. Nearly 12 inches (30 centimeters) of snow fell at Donner Pass, northwest of Lake Tahoe, on November 13, according to the Central Sierra Snow Laboratory . The accumulation snarled traffic on Interstate 80 in the area, prompting officials to close the highway in both directions that evening. To the south, the ski resort at Mammoth Mountain reported 9 to 13 inches (23 to 33 centimeters) of new snow, and officials at Yosemite National Park closed several roads ahead of the storm. More wet weather and mountain snow are forecast to follow . The National Weather Service (NWS) issued a winter storm warning for portions of the Sierras above 5,000 feet (1,500 meters) in elevation from November 18 to 20. NWS warned of difficult-to-impossible travel conditions, gusty winds, and snow accumulations of around 4 feet (120 centimeters) possible above 8,000 feet (2,400 meters). She talks about being criticised for her support of Israel and pushed to the limit by Lars von Trier While she was making the film Women on Trial , about the real-life trial of a child prosecuted for having an abortion, someone sent Charlotte Gainsbourg a photograph of her mother at one of the pro-choice demonstrations that erupted in France at the time. It was “very moving”, says Gainsbourg to see her mother, the actor Jane Birkin, in 1972, “looking beautiful and in the middle of a demonstration”. At that time, in a court in Bobigny, a Paris suburb, the prominent lawyer Gisèle Halimi was defending 16-year-old Marie-Claire Chevalier, as well as her mother and two other women who helped her have an abortion, then illegal in France. The Bobigny trial was new to her, says Gainsbourg, who plays Halimi, a leading figure in French feminism and activism who died in 2020. “I had no idea. About World Vision Iraq World Vision Iraq (WV Iraq) has operated since 2014 across Erbil, Kirkuk, Ninewa, Salah al‑Din, Anbar, and Thi‑Qar, partnering with government, local NGOs, and the private sector to reduce climate and disaster risks and protect children and vulnerable households. noticias.contenido: Country: Iraq Source: World Vision Please refer to the attached file. About World Vision Iraq World Vision Iraq (WV Iraq) has operated since 2014 across Erbil, Kirkuk, Ninewa, Salah al‑Din, Anbar, and Thi‑Qar, partnering with government, local NGOs, and the private sector to reduce climate and disaster risks and protect children and vulnerable households. We combine disaster risk reduction (DRR), climate adaptation, water security, and resilient livelihoods to deliver sustainable results in fragile settings. Context Iraq is among the countries most vulnerable to climate change. Its geographical location makes it particularly susceptible to various hydrological, meteorological, and climatological risks due to its arid climate and downstream position. In recent years, Iraq has recorded its lowest rainfall in two decades, leading to water scarcity, below-average vegetation growth, and reduced crop yields. These challenges worsen existing vulnerabilities, especially among marginalized communities. Our approaches The primary objective of WV Iraqʼs Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience programming is to strengthen community resilience against disasters and ensure a safer environment for children by addressing the underlying drivers of risk and vulnerability in a changing climate. WV Iraq has a strong track record in disaster risk management and anticipatory action. Our expertise includes: Risk Assessment and Early Warning Systems We conduct climate and disaster risk analyses Capacity Statement to produce community risk maps and establish practical early warning protocols with clear activation triggers for anticipatory actions such as inputs, and asset protection. Scenario‑based plans and crisis modifiers enable fast, adaptive responses across humanitarian, development, and peace programmes. Community-Based Disaster Risk Management (CBDRM) We prioritize building the capacity of vulnerable communities to prepare for and respond to disasters. This includes training community members on disaster preparedness, establishing community-based disaster management committees, and conducting drills and simulations. Resilient livelihoods We promote climate-resilient livelihoods through CSA practices, including Farmer Field Schools, conservation agriculture, efficient irrigation, and improved seed and soil management. Financial resilience is supported through S4T groups and financial literacy, complemented by private-sector partnerships that expand access to inputs and services. Integrated water resources management We promote sustainable water management by implementing multiple-use water systems that serve domestic needs, agriculture, livestock, and livelihoods, ensuring equitable access and long-term resource protection. We also strengthen WASH committees by training them to manage water and sanitation services safely and efficiently, engage communities, and uphold environmental safeguards.

COP31 - ANTALYA, TÜRKIYE - 9 - 20 NOVEMBER 2026 CONTEXT AND NEED: Iraq is among the countries most severely impacted by climate change, experiencing significant water scarcity, and rapid desertification, leading to the annual loss of 60,000 acres of arable land. The country faces soaring temperatures, diminishing rainfall, intensified droughts, frequent sand and dust storms, and periodic flooding. These issues are exacerbated by rapid population growth, urbanization, and regional political instability, which impede effective water management and sustainable development. Consequently, there is a growing crisis of climate-induced migration, with more than 186,000 already displaced. Urgent, coordinated action from the Iraqi government, international actors, and local communities is required to mitigate impacts, enhance resilience, and address these multifaceted threats.

noticias.titulo: Photon fluctuations offer new way to probe electron dynamics in crystals
noticias.resumen: Intense laser light can make a crystal emit new colors at frequencies many times higher than that of the original beam. This process, known as high-harmonic generation, provides a powerful way to investigate the rapid motion of electrons in solids. Researchers usually study the brightness and spectrum of the emitted light. Yet those measurements capture only part of the available information. Fluctuations between individual laser pulses can also reveal how the emission is produced.

noticias.contenido: Country: Afghanistan Source: World Bank Please refer to the attached file. Strong Harvest Lifts Afghanistan’s Economy, but Falling Incomes and Water Shortages Strain Families KABUL, November 18, 2026 — Afghanistan’s economy is expected to grow by 3 percent in 2026, driven almost entirely by a strong harvest. However, output per person is set to fall by 3.3 percent, its third consecutive annual decline, as the population is projected to grow by 6.6 percent, according to the World Bank’s latest Afghanistan Development Update . The Fall 2026 report, which includes a special focus on water security, finds that many families are under pressure, while the country’s water reserves are shrinking. Fewer workdays and higher food prices have reduced what families can afford. In September 2026, casual laborers found 14 percent fewer days of work than a year earlier, while their weekly earnings bought 27 percent less wheat flour. And despite the improved harvest, an estimated 15.9 million people faced acute food insecurity in September and October 2026, according to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC). Domestic revenue rose by 10.2 percent in the first half of 2026 as domestic taxes and non-tax revenue offset a fall in customs duties. Public investment remains low, with capital spending projected at about 1.3 percent of GDP for the fiscal year. With the border with Pakistan closed, about 97 percent of Afghanistan’s imports now enter through Central Asia and Iran. Exports fell by 15.1 percent in April–September 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier. The report also finds that Afghanistan has lost an estimated 4.9 billion cubic meters of freshwater reserves a year since 2003. In Kabul, groundwater is being drawn nearly four times as fast as it is naturally replenished. Water shortages are also putting rural livelihoods at risk. Agriculture accounts for 46 percent of employment and 95 percent of water withdrawals. Looking ahead, economic growth is projected to reach 3.3 percent in 2027 and 3.5 percent in 2028. Even under this projected recovery, output per person in 2028 is expected to remain about 7 percent below its 2024 level. A poor harvest, further disruptions to trade routes, additional large-scale returns, or deeper aid cuts could weaken the outlook. The report identifies more reliable trade routes, expanded employment in provinces receiving large numbers of returnees, and restored access to education and work for women and girls as priorities for improving living standards. On water, it calls for restoring essential water and sanitation services, repairing irrigation systems, and protecting watersheds and groundwater reserves. About the Afghanistan Development Update: The Afghanistan Development Update is part of the World Bank’s ongoing research, monitoring, and analytical work on Afghanistan’s economy and society. It aims to support evidence-based policymaking and inform the international community on economic developments in Afghanistan. Contacts In Kabul Payamulhaq Barrai pbarrai@worldbankgroup.org In Washington Serene Jweied sjweied@worldbankgroup.org

noticias.contenido: Country: Ukraine Source: European Commission Please refer to the attached file. €237.6 billion in overall support to Ukraine and Ukrainians including €3.8 billion from the proceeds of Russian immobilised assets The EU stands united in its unwavering support for Ukraine in the face of Russia’s war of aggression and its illegal attempts to annex Ukrainian territory. The EU continues to work relentlessly with international partners to make sure Ukraine receives the material support it needs and to hold Russia accountable for its actions. The EU has also offered temporary protection to over four million people fleeing the war and is committed to continue providing strong political, financial, economic, humanitarian, military and diplomatic support to Ukraine and its people for as long as it takes . The EU opened accession negotiations with Ukraine. SUPPORT FOR UKRAINE’S ECONOMY The EU has established the Ukraine Facility of up to €50 billion to provide predictable and flexible support to Ukraine for the period 2024-2027 to support recovery, reconstruction and modernisation, in line with its EU path. So far, a total amount of more than €31.4 billion of direct assistance to Ukraine has been provided (excluding external contributions). The total EU commitments under the Ukraine Investment Framework now reach €8.5 billion , expecting to leverage over €25.7 billion in investments. The EU set up a €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan for 2026 and 2027 , based on EU borrowing on the capital markets backed by the EU budget headroom. Two thirds are indicatively dedicated to defence procurement support, and one third to overall budgetary assistance. €25.8 billion has been disbursed so far, of which €6.9 billion as macro-financial assistance, €18.1 billion for defence procurement, and €800 million channelled through the Ukraine Facility, following the satisfactorily completion of reforms. In 2025 , following up on the commitments by G7 leaders and based on a proposal by the Commission, the EU adopted and disbursed a financial assistance package consisting of an exceptional macro-financial assistance (MFA) loan of €18.1 billion . As part of the package, a loan cooperation mechanism is financed by extraordinary revenues stemming from immobilised Russian sovereign assets. On 29 October 2025 the EU-Ukraine Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Area entered into force. In 2023 , the EU budget enabled €19.5 billion in assistance to Ukraine, including an unprecedented support package of €18 billion for MFA+. Furthermore, the EU mobilised €1 billion for fast recovery, while guarantee agreements were signed with international financial institutions with potential capacity to unlock over €800 million in investments from the Ukrainian private sector for the recovery and reconstruction of the country’s economy. In 2022 , a total of €11.6 billion was provided in loans and grants. These helped Ukraine keep paying wages and pensions, restore critical infrastructure that is destroyed by the war, maintain essential public services, such as hospitals, schools, and housing for relocated people, and ensure overall macroeconomic stability.

noticias.autor: UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights
noticias.contenido: Country: Ukraine Source: UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights Please refer to the attached file. In Ukraine Civilians Die at Alarming Rates Amid Intensifying Attacks, UN Human Rights Officials Say Kyiv, November 17, 2026 -- Powerful weapons of war kill ever growing numbers of civilians across Ukraine, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU) said today. Attacks in October alone left at least 372 civilians dead and 1,981 injured HRMMU reported in its monthly update. The report notes that the number of killed and injured in October of this year was 95 per cent higher than in October 2025. The latest figures show that this year has seen significantly higher casualties than previous years. The alarming trend continued in November which saw one of the deadliest single attacks for civilians since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion. On 2 November multiple bombs struck the premises of a school, including an underground shelter in Komyshuvakha in south-eastern Ukraine, where civilians had gathered to receive humanitarian assistance. Ukrainian authorities announced on 16 November that 72 people had died in the attack and that four others were still missing. HRMMU continues to verify the identity and status of those killed, but has already confirmed that dozens of them were civilians, including local residents, local administration staff and emergency workers. "The first ten months of this year have seen more civilian deaths than all of 2025, which in turn was worse than the year before," said Danielle Bell who heads HRMMU. "The world should not become numb to the deadly toll the war exacts on Ukraine's civilians," she said. Long-range weapons (missiles and drones) remain the leading cause of civilian casualties, accounting for more than half of those killed and injured. In October, casualties from aerial glide bombs increased, with the number of civilians killed doubling compared with September, reaching 92 killed and 331 injured. Aerial glide bombs and short-range drones accounted for nearly equal shares of civilian casualties, 18 and 19 per cent, respectively. In October, Russian armed forces significantly intensified attacks on energy infrastructure across Ukraine as the country braces for its fifth winter at war. The attacks damaged electricity and heating infrastructure, temporarily disrupting power and, in some cities, also water supply, forcing Ukrainian authorities to introduce rolling power outages across the country. Ukrainian armed forces also attacked electricity infrastructure in Russian-occupied territory of Ukraine. Meanwhile according to public statements by Russian authorities on individual incidents in October, at least 90 people were killed and 306 injured in occupied territory and at least 59 people were killed and 402 injured in the Russian Federation as a result of Ukrainian attacks, but HRMMU is not able to verify the figures because of lack of access and independent sources of information. In territory of Ukraine occupied by Russia HRMMU verified that at least 12 civilians were killed and 18 injured. In all 17,994 civilians have been killed and 57,854 have been injured in Ukraine since Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February of 2022. Note: HRMMU will publish its findings related to the attack in Komyshuvakha in due course. For media inquiries, please contact Kris Janowski, Spokesperson +380952300437, krzysztof.janowski@un.org

noticias.contenido: Country: Sudan Source: World Health Organization 17 November 2026, Khartoum, Sudan – The World Health Organization (WHO) is calling for sustained support to keep essential health services functioning in Sudan’s White Nile and North Kordofan states, where conflict, displacement, disease outbreaks and shortages of medicines and power continue to strain the health system. The call follows a WHO mission to Kosti in White Nile State, and to El Obeid, North Kordofan’s capital, from 7 to 12 November, led by WHO Representative in Sudan Dr Abdinasir Abubakar. “The health needs I witnessed in White Nile and North Kordofan are immense. We urgently need to scale up essential health services in peripheral localities and displacement camps,” said Dr Abdinasir. “Despite enormous challenges, health workers and partners remain committed to serving the most vulnerable communities. We must match their commitment with sustained support.” Prolonged conflict, displacement, food insecurity, disease outbreaks and malnutrition have severely disrupted health services. Across Sudan, 21 million people need health assistance, while 37% of health facilities are non-functional. The mission highlighted continuing gaps in electricity supplies, medicines, operational resources and access to care in both states. Power interruptions continue to disrupt critical services, including operating theatres, intensive care, neonatal incubators, oxygen generation, blood banks, dialysis and laboratory services, putting patients at risk. Reliable power, including solarization, is urgently needed to sustain lifesaving services. White Nile State hosts more than 216 000 internally displaced people and nearly 455 000 refugees – approximately half of Sudan’s refugee population – placing considerable pressure on already strained health services. In North Kordofan, prolonged conflict, displacement, food insecurity and economic hardship are exacerbating health and nutrition needs. El Obeid hosts most of the over 141 000 internally displaced people in Sheikan locality, further straining already overstretched health services. WHO support to Kosti Teaching Hospital reached more than 24 000 people between November 2025 and April 2026. WHO also supported oxygen-cylinder refills, provided three oxygen concentrators and installed solar capacity in the Emergency Department. A separate solar system at Kosti Renal Dialysis Centre is helping sustain lifesaving emergency dialysis services during frequent power outages. In El Obeid, WHO support in 2025–2026 has contributed to approximately 344 500 health services, including 90 000 patient consultations. WHO also provided over 9000 litres of fuel to help maintain electricity at El Obeid Teaching Hospital, alongside medicines, supplies, capacity-building and operational support. During the mission, Dr Abdinasir met with state government officials, health authorities, WHO teams and humanitarian partners to review priority needs and ongoing humanitarian response and recovery interventions. In Kosti, he opened a training workshop on Ebola virus disease preparedness, and in El Obeid he joined the monthly Health Cluster meeting with six health partners to strengthen coordination and the collective health response. WHO calls for urgent, sustained flexible funding to maintain and expand essential health services, support frontline health workers, strengthen outbreak preparedness and response and ensure reliable medical supplies, power and emergency referral systems. Safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access and the protection of health workers, patients and health facilities are also crucial. WHO continues to work with health authorities, communities, Health Cluster partners and donors to sustain lifesaving services and support the recovery of Sudan’s health system.

noticias.autor: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
noticias.contenido: Country: Côte d'Ivoire Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Please refer to the attached file. FOOD SECURITY SNAPSHOT Cereal production forecast above average in 2026 Prices of rice near or below year-earlier levels About 1.3 million people severely acute food insecure during 2026 lean season Cereal production forecast above average in 2026 In southern bimodal rainfall areas, harvesting of the 2026 main season maize and rice crops was completed in September. Generally favorable weather conditions between March and July 2026 supported crop establishment and development. However, heavy rains in June and July triggered localized flooding, particularly around Abidjan, damaging crops in some areas. Planting of the secondary-season maize and rice crops was also completed in September. Below-average cumulative precipitation amounts between September and October constrained planting operations and early crop development in several areas. Weather forecasts indicate a high likelihood of above-average rainfall amounts in November across most producing regions, which are expected to improve crop conditions, while increasing the risk of localized flooding. By contrast, below-average precipitation amounts are forecast in some minor producing coastal areas. In northern unimodal rainfall areas, harvesting of the 2026 coarse grain and rice crops is underway and expected to conclude by year-end. The May-October rainy season started on time or up to three weeks earlier than usual in some areas, supporting planting operations and crop establishment. Near-average cumulative rainfall amounts through October were generally conducive to crop development, and production prospects are favorable. Aggregate cereal production in 2026 is preliminarily forecast at about 4.4 million tonnes, approximately 20 percent above the average of the previous five years. The good output mainly reflects an expansion in planted area, officially estimated at 25 percent above average, supported by government programmes providing agricultural inputs and machinery to farmers in collaboration with technical and financial partners. Prices of rice near or below year-earlier levels Prices of locally produced rice, a key staple food, were generally stable between June and September 2026, with seasonal increases of up to 5 percent recorded in some markets. Despite these increases, prices in September were near or up to 10 percent below their year-earlier levels across monitored markets. About 1.3 million people severely acute food insecure during 2026 lean season According to the latest Cadre Harmonisé (CH) analysis, about 1.3 million people (5 percent of the analysed population) were estimated to face severe acute food insecurity (CH Phase 3 [Crisis] and above) during the June-August 2026 lean season, including more than 14 500 people in CH Phase 4 (Emergency). This represents a slight improvement from the same period in 2025, when approximately 1.4 million people (6 percent of the analysed population) were estimated to face CH Phase 3 (Crisis) and above. Spillover effects of the conflict in the Central Sahel remain a major driver of acute food insecurity in northern areas, particularly in the Tchologo and Bounkani regions, where 12 and 14 percent of the analysed population, respectively, were estimated to be in CH Phase 3 (Crisis) and above. These regions host about 85 percent of the country’s 88 000 registered refugees and asylum seekers, while continued arrivals from Burkina Faso and Mali are placing additional pressure on natural resources and livelihoods in host communities. Persistent insecurity in border areas is also restricting access to farmland and pastures and disrupting food supplies to local markets, where elevated prices have been reported. Households’ economic access to food also remains a concern. The guaranteed farmgate price of cocoa, the country’s main export crop, for the 2026/27 main marketing season is 57 percent below the level set at the start of the previous marketing season and is expected to reduce incomes among households dependent on cocoa production. In addition, recent increases in domestic diesel prices, linked to high international oil prices, have raised transport costs and may exert upward pressure on food prices, further constraining households’ purchasing power. Flooding in southern areas affected about 21 500 people in 2026 and caused damage to homes, productive assets, crops and road infrastructure. The resulting disruptions to trade flows and market supplies contributed to localized food price increases.
etiquetas: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

noticias.contenido: Country: Haiti Source: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification Please refer to the attached file. Vue d’ensemble L’analyse de la situation nutritionnelle révèle une situation précaire sur l’ensemble du territoire avec une prédominance des zones en situation d’Alerte nutritionnelle. Pour la période de juin à novembre 2026, les communes d’Arcahaie, Cabaret et Cité Soleil se trouvent en situation nutritionnelle Sérieuse (Phase 3 de l’IPC), principalement à cause de la situation sécuritaire, de l’insécurité alimentaire persistante et du poids des phénomènes morbides. Par ailleurs, 59 communes sont placées en état d’Alerte nutritionnelle (Phase 2 de l’IPC), tandis que cinq départements et sept communes affichent une situation Acceptable (Phase 1 de l’IPC). Pour la période projetée de décembre 2026 à mai 2027, une nette dégradation de la situation nutritionnelle est attendue en lien avec une dégradation probable des conditions sécuritaires, socio-politiques, épidémiologiques et climatiques. Les communes de Cabaret et Cité Soleil basculeront en situation Critique (Phase 4 de l’IPC), tandis qu’Arcahaie est susceptible de se maintenir en situation Sérieuse (Phase 3 de l’IPC), rejointe par 28 autres communes qui quitteront la phase d’Alerte pour la phase Sérieuse. Parallèlement, les départements des Nippes, du Nord-Est et du Sud-Est, ainsi que cinq communes, passeront de la situation Acceptable à la situation d’Alerte, où se maintiennent déjà 31 autres communes. En revanche, la situation restera Acceptable (Phase 1 de l’IPC) pour les départements du Nord et du Sud, ainsi que pour deux communes du département de l’Ouest. Par ailleurs, sur la période de juin 2026 à mai 2027, plus de 253 700cas de malnutrition aiguë globale (modérée et sévère) sont attendus chez les enfants de 6 à 59 mois. Parmi eux, près de 93 900 enfants risquent de souffrir de malnutrition aiguë sévère, une forme particulièrement critique qui augmente fortement le risque de mortalité. Il est enfin important de noter que l’analyse n’a pas permis d’examiner de manière désagrégée certains groupes particulièrement vulnérables, notamment les personnes déplacées internes (PDI). Une mise à jour plus granulaire apparaît donc nécessaire afin de mieux appréhender leurs vulnérabilités spécifiques et d’orienter plus efficacement les interventions en fonction de leurs besoins. La réalisation rapide d’une enquête nutritionnelle est indispensable pour mesurer l’ampleur de la crise et optimiser le déploiement des interventions d’aide. Partout dans le pays, l’impact direct de la crise sécuritaire avec les déplacements de population et l’insécurité alimentaire persistante, exacerbée par les chocs climatiques et la crise économique, dégrade fortement la situation nutritionnelle. À cela s’ajoutent des déterminants majeurs tels que la forte morbidité infantile (paludisme, diarrhées, infections respiratoires) et les épidémies récurrentes de choléra, ainsi que les carences liées à l’alimentation et aux pratiques de soin (faiblesse de l’allaitement maternel exclusif). La deuxième édition de l’analyse IPC de la malnutrition aiguë (IPC MNA) en Haïti a couvert l’ensemble des 10 départements du pays. L’analyse a été menée à l’échelle départementale pour les Nippes, le Nord, le Nord-Est, le Sud et le Sud-Est, tandis qu’elle s’est faite à l’échelle communale (couvrant 69 communes) pour l’Artibonite, le Centre, la Grand’Anse, l’Ouest et le Nord-Ouest. Les facteurs contributifs à cette situation nutritionnelle précaire varient selon les zones analysées. Dans les zones classées en Phase 3 de l’IPC, les principaux facteurs contributifs sont l’insécurité résiduelle, la précarité de la consommation alimentaire des enfants et l’insécurité alimentaire persistante. S’y ajoutent une forte prévalence des infections respiratoires aiguës et de la fièvre, la faiblesse de la couverture sanitaire ainsi que de mauvaises conditions d’hygiène.

noticias.autor: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
noticias.contenido: Countries: South Sudan, Ethiopia Source: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies Please refer to the attached file. Description of the Event Date when the trigger was met 23-12-2025 What happened, where and when? The Marburg Virus Disease (MVD) outbreak was declared in Ethiopia on 14 November 2025, prompting heightened preparedness measures in neighboring South Sudan due to the risk of cross-border transmission through frequent population movement, trade, and pastoral migration. On 23 December 2025, three suspected MVD-related deaths were reported in Kapoeta East County, including two individuals with a recent travel history to the affected areas of Ethiopia and one suspected community-linked case. These alerts triggered increased preparedness and readiness efforts by the South Sudan Red Cross (SSRC) in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and partners. The operation was implemented from 30 December 2025 to 28 February 2026 in the high-risk border counties of Akobo, Maiwut, Pibor, and Kapoeta East, which had been identified as priority locations because of their proximity to Ethiopia and high levels of cross-border movement. Preparedness activities included volunteer training, community-based surveillance, risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), infection prevention and control (IPC), hygiene promotion, and Safe and Dignified Burial (SDB) preparedness. During implementation, the epidemiological situation remained stable and no confirmed MVD cases were reported in South Sudan. Investigations into suspected alerts, including those reported in Kapoeta East, did not result in any confirmed Marburg cases, and one suspected alert investigated during the operation tested negative. However, operational challenges affected implementation. In Akobo and Maiwut, insecurity and localized conflict restricted access to some communities and required volunteers and staff to relocate temporarily to safer locations while continuing awareness activities where feasible. In Pibor, cattle-raiding incidents disrupted planned interventions and limited access to some target areas. In Kapoeta East, poor road conditions and the remoteness of border communities presented logistical challenges, although SSRC successfully reached border locations, trained volunteers, and implemented preparedness activities. By the end of the operation, no confirmed MVD cases had been detected in South Sudan. The outbreak situation in Ethiopia had improved, transmission had been brought under control, and preparedness capacities in the targeted counties had been strengthened through trained volunteers, community awareness, surveillance systems, IPC measures, and SDB readiness mechanisms.
etiquetas: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies

noticias.titulo: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
noticias.resumen: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint now live inside Copilot; always-on agents are next.
noticias.contenido: Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company's vision for its new "frontier ecosystem," announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as "the new OS for work." The announcement is a striking inversion of how we've traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent's work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications. noticias.contenido: Country: Afghanistan Source: Save the Children KABUL, 18 November 2026 – More than half of children displaced in Afghanistan said they have less food to eat since leaving their homes, while two in five reported worsening health, according to a new Save the Children report that reveals the severe toll displacement is taking on children across the country. The “Children on the Move” report, based on interviews with more than 800 children and caregivers in seven provinces in Afghanistan, found that displacement over the past three years has deepened hunger, disrupted education and exposed children to heightened protection risks. More than nine in 10 children surveyed had experienced displacement or migration. More than half (55%) of children said they had less food to eat after moving, 41% said their health had deteriorated, and a third (33%) of caregivers said children's access to education had worsened. But despite growing needs, support is failing to reach many children. Fewer than one in 10 children surveyed said they had received any assistance, while nine in 10 said they needed support to access food. The findings come after more than 6.67 million Afghans have returned from Pakistan and Iran since September 2023 – increasing the population by up to 14% - and putting greater pressure on families and communities already struggling with poverty, food insecurity and repeated crises. [2]. Afghanistan also has one of the highest rates of internal displacement globally, with about 7 million people , or around 14% of the population, displaced as of 2025. [3]. Economic hardship is the main driver of displacement in Afghanistan. Nearly half of children (49%) said their families moved because they could not find work or earn enough income, while a third cited food shortages. Almost one in four said their families had relocated due to deportation or pressure to leave another country. Nearly seven out of 10 children surveyed have endured two or more crises in the last three years, including drought, floods, earthquakes and conflict. Compounding crises and displacement are affecting children’s wellbeing in Afghanistan, with children facing growing protection risks. Just over one in 10 (11%) said they had been exposed to at least one protection risk, including child labour, physical or verbal violence or early marriage. Caregivers reported that girls faced particularly high risks during displacement journeys and after arriving in new locations. Among those affected is Nooria*, 8, who arrived in Afghanistan for this first time earlier this year after her family left Pakistan where they had built their lives over five decades. Nooria*, her parents and three siblings arrived with little more than the clothes they carried. Nooria* said: “We returned from Pakistan. We had a home there, and I had many friends. I like Afghanistan too, but I miss my school and my friends. We used to play together and laugh a lot. “We want to have a school like the one we had in Pakistan, where we can continue our education.” Nooria’s family cannot afford the transport costs to send her to school, but she attends classes at a Save the Children temporary learning space. Her mother, Nazoo*, 28, said: “My husband does not have a job here, and we have no source of income to provide for our children's needs. I worry every day about how we will find food for our next meal. “When you are born in a country and get married there, that place becomes your home. You feel that you belong there. When you suddenly have to leave, your whole life falls apart, especially when you arrive with nothing.” The ‘Children on the Move’ report found that assistance reaching children is extremely limited, with significant gaps between needs and the support they receive. Ashish Damle, Country Director, Save the Children in Afghanistan said: “No child should have to abandon their homes, schools and communities for safety or survival - but for many, displacement has become part of their childhood. Children face dangerous journeys with serious protection risks, only to arrive in places where their families are still struggling to put food on the table, access healthcare and send them to school. “Our ‘Children on the Move’ research reveals a deeply concerning reality - finding a new home does not mean reaching safety. Girls and children with disabilities in particular face greater protection risks, while poverty is forcing families to make impossible choices just to survive, often with little or no humanitarian assistance. “Children who have already lost their homes should not be left to face these risks alone. We urgently need sustained funding to protect them along migration routes and ensure they can access essential services wherever they settle. “These children deserve more than day to day survival. They deserve the chance to feel safe, return to school and rebuild their lives.” Save the Children has been working in Afghanistan since 1976, including through periods of conflict, displacement and natural disasters. We currently run programmes in nine provinces and work with partners across an additional 11 provinces, delivering services in health, nutrition, education, child protection, shelter, water, sanitation, hygiene and livelihoods. Save the Children’s ‘Children on the Move’ study in Afghanistan was conducted in selected locations affected by floods, droughts, earthquakes, and conflict, identified as migration source, transit, and destination areas. The primary study population was children on the move aged 0–17 years and their families. 824 children and 838 caregivers were interviewed through structured questionnaires and 32 qualitative consultations conducted with key informants and caregiver groups in July 2026. noticias.contenido: Country: Syrian Arab Republic Source: European Commission Please refer to the attached file. Today, the Syria Partnership Coordination Forum (SPCF) convened in Damascus for the first time to advance Syria's recovery and reconstruction, showcase investment opportunities and agree on concrete steps forward. The SPCF brought together key partners, including EU Member States, the G7, Arab countries, and the UN and International Financial Institutions, such as the World Bank, the European Investment Bank, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the Islamic Development Bank, as well as civil society, to discuss Syria's business environment and steps to translate Syria's priorities into concrete investment opportunities. The Forum, co-chaired by Syria and the EU, was opened by Commissioner for the Mediterranean Dubravka Šuica and the Syrian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Assaad Al-Shaibani. Economic revitalisation, institutional recovery and improved livelihoods In her second visit to the country, Commissioner Šuica officially launched the Syria Technical Assistance Hub to support Syrian institutions in strengthening their capacities and advancing reforms that are instrumental to restore confidence, attract responsible investment and support sustainable economic recovery. The Commissioner also witnessed the signing of new EU-funded contracts supporting Syria's recovery and reconstruction, namely on the rule of law, on an enabling business environment andon support to small and medium-sized enterprises . These initiatives will help revive the economy, strengthen public institutions and improve livelihoods. By helping businesses access finance and grow, the projects can create jobs and improve conditions for investment. They will also improve access to justice, supporting a recovery that benefits people across Syria. During her bilateral meeting with Minister Al-Shaibani, Commissioner Šuica received Syria's signed undertaking to implement the EU's Registered Exporter system . This marks an important step towards enabling Syrian products to benefit from preferential access to the EU market under the Generalised Scheme of Preferences, opening up new opportunities for Syrian exporters and supporting the country's economic recovery. Commissioner Šuica also visited the Deir Ali Power Plant together with Ibrahim Al-Adhan, Syrian Deputy Minister of Energy and EIB Vice President Gelsomina Vigliotti. The visit highlighted the importance of restoring Syria's energy infrastructure for economic recovery and explored opportunities for future EU engagement in the energy sector with other international partners. Background After the fall of the Assad regime at the end of December 2024 and following the Brussels IX Conference of 17 March 2025, Syria and the EU launched the SPCF, which provides a platform to align partners' support on Syria's recovery priorities and coordinate on their implementation. The Forum is instrumental in facilitating structured engagement among key partners, including EU Member States, the G7, Arab nations, and International Financial Institutions. The SPCF is structured under regular senior-official plenary meetings at capital level, and regular practical level. It builds on the EU's support for Syria's recovery. During her first visit to Damascus in June 2025, Commissioner Šuica announced €175 million to help Syria rebuild its institutions, advance transitional justice and revive its economy. In January 2026, President Ursula von der Leyen announced around €620 million in EU support for 2026–2027 to support recovery and provide humanitarian aid. In May 2026, the Council restored the full application of the EU–Syria Cooperation Agreement, paving the way for stronger trade ties. On 16 November 2026, EU Foreign Ministers supported moving ahead with the EU-Syria Association Agreement. In December, a Day of Dialogue will take place for the second time in Damascus, organised by the Syrian authorities, Syrian civil society and the EU. It will provide a platform for inclusive dialogue on Syria's transition and the role of civil society. For more information EU support to Syria - factsheet The EU announces €175 million to support recovery in Syria EU opens new chapter in its relations with Syria Quote(s) A peaceful, stable and inclusive Syria is important for Syrians, to the region and to Europe. The EU is ready to deepen its partnership with Syria as Syrians rebuild their country for all citizens. At today’s Forum in Damascus, we focused on what international partners and businesses can do to support the country’s own priorities, so people can find jobs, businesses can reopen and services can further be restored. Dubravka Šuica, Commissioner for the Mediterranean Contacts for media Guillaume MERCIER Spokesperson Phone +32 2 298 05 64 Mail guillaume.mercier@ec.europa.eu Luca DILDA Press Officer Phone +32 2 295 21 53 Mail luca.dilda@ec.europa.eu

noticias.titulo: Rare encounter with isolated Indigenous Awá people in Brazil exposes vulnerability
noticias.resumen: On Nov. 16, a group of roughly 20 Indigenous Awá people living in voluntary isolation approached an Indigenous Guajajara village, in Brazil’s northeastern Maranhão state. The rare encounter has mobilized Indigenous peoples and activists concerned about the safety of the Awá, considered the most threatened group on the planet. The motivation for the unusual interaction […]
noticias.contenido: On Nov. 16, a group of roughly 20 Indigenous Awá people living in voluntary isolation approached an Indigenous Guajajara village, in Brazil’s northeastern Maranhão state. The rare encounter has mobilized Indigenous peoples and activists concerned about the safety of the Awá, considered the most threatened group on the planet. The motivation for the unusual interaction is unclear, but Guajajara leaders “expressed concern about the physical condition of some members of the group, especially children and older people, who appeared to be very thin,” according to accounts and images posted on social media by Indigenous organizations. The Guajajara reportedly offered the Awá food and other objects; the Awá remained there briefly before returning to the forest. Brazil’s Indigenous affairs agency, Funai, told Mongabay by email that technical teams are monitoring the situation and that it had activated a contingency plan to “ensure that the relevant agencies are prepared to respond appropriately to any developments in the situation, especially regarding the ethno-environmental protection, health and safety of the Indigenous people involved.” Funai added that the peoples’ right to self-determination would continue to be respected. Unlike other isolated peoples who make frequent contact, this is the first time in decades that the Awá of the Arariboia Indigenous Territory “have appeared in this way and made such close contact with other people,” Sarah Shenker, director and senior researcher at the Indigenous rights organization Survival International Brazil, told Mongabay by phone. noticias.titulo: Turning food waste into insect feed poses only low mad cow disease risk
noticias.resumen: Insects can convert food waste and by-products from the food industry (such as unsold ready meals or slaughter by-products) into ingredients for animal feed. In this way, they can contribute to the transition toward a circular food production system, in which what would otherwise be wasted is reused. However, these waste streams may contain animal proteins that pose a risk of transmitting diseases such as bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), also known as mad cow disease. For this reason, rearing insects on waste streams containing animal proteins is not permitted in the European Union.

noticias.contenido: Researchers from Chile's Institute of Ecology and Biodiversity (IEB) have developed a multiobjective model to identify priority areas for large-scale ecological restoration in Chile, South America. noticias.titulo: Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors
noticias.resumen: Malware cocktail delivers cryptocurrency theft payloads and iOS exploits, among other things.
noticias.contenido: Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday. ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers. Other components skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and, on iPhones and iPads, delivered iOS exploit kits known as Coruna and DarkSword. Optimizely infrastructure delivers multipurpose malware Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both company code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript. Read full article Comments

noticias.titulo: Indiana court upholds extra approval for 32-home Crooked Lake project with shared access
noticias.resumen: A proposed residential project near Crooked Lake has faced significant legal hurdles over access rights to the waterfront for numerous homes. Local residents expressed concerns regarding potential overuse of a single dock for entry. The Steuben County Plan Commission mandated that a special exception be obtained, a ruling the developer challenged. However, the Indiana Court of Appeals upheld the commission's directive, reinforcing the need to adhere to zoning laws.

noticias.titulo: Bird flu wiped out the Sandwich tern colony in 2022, three years later, 756 of them have returned
noticias.resumen: After suffering from High Pathogenic Avian Influenza in 2022, the Sandwich tern colony at Pagham Harbour faced severe population loss. Through extensive conservation efforts, the colony saw a remarkable recovery, breeding 756 pairs by 2026. This comeback has also benefited other bird species, such as black-headed gulls and avocets. RSPB rangers and volunteers have played a crucial role in habitat management and safety.
